summary: This endpoint is a live-verified geography aggregation surface for disaster-designated spending. State-level obligation and outlay stories are reverified and remain the strongest safe path; county, district, and face_value_of_loan remain documented but not re-probed in this repair.
businessPurpose: Use this endpoint to answer where disaster-designated federal spending was directed geographically for a chosen DEFC set and spending measure, especially for state maps, explicitly sorted ranking lists, and per-capita comparisons.
analyticalGrain: One row per returned geography shape_code at the requested geo_layer and scope, with a live-observed uncoded aggregate bucket when geography assignment is missing and geo_layer_filters are omitted. Current live confidence is strongest for the state layer, while county and district should be treated as documented-but-not-reverified.

primaryEntities.name: disaster geography aggregate
primaryEntities.description: A rolled-up spending record for one geography code at the selected state, county, or district layer after applying disaster filters.

primaryEntities.name: DEFC-filtered award population
primaryEntities.description: The set of awards included in the geography rollup, defined primarily by filter.def_codes and optionally narrowed by award type. Shared passthrough filters appear in the retired low-level artifact but were not reliable geography-bounding controls in this repair's live evidence.

measures.name: amount
measures.description: Summed dollars for the requested spending_type, such as obligation, outlay, or face value of loan.

measures.name: award_count
measures.description: Number of awards contributing to each geography total.

measures.name: per_capita
measures.description: Per-capita geography metric derived from amount and population when population is available.

dimensions.name: geography layer
dimensions.description: Choose state, county, or district to set the response grain and the interpretation of shape_code. State is the strongest current live-verified path; county and district remain documented but not re-probed in this repair and should carry an explicit confidence warning.

dimensions.name: geographic scope
dimensions.description: Switch between recipient location and place of performance geography before aggregating the spending.

dimensions.name: DEFC code
dimensions.description: Disaster Emergency Fund Codes determine which disaster-designated spending population is included. This geography endpoint does not translate those codes into plain-language labels, and the promoted semantic MCP surface reviewed for this repair did not expose a promoted semantic DEFC reference endpoint. Treat GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ or the published DEFC reference as an external/raw fallback before writing plain-language analysis.

dimensions.name: award type
dimensions.description: Optional award_type_codes can narrow the rollup to contracts, grants, loans, and related award categories.

dimensions.name: time period and recipient filters
dimensions.description: The retired low-level artifact carries shared keys such as time_period, recipient_scope, and recipient_locations, but a 2026-05-15 live probe accepted those fields without materially narrowing the sampled DEFC L state rollup, so they are not reliable geography-bounding controls here.

suitableQuestions.name: Which states received the most disaster obligations for a DEFC?
suitableQuestions.description: Use geo_layer=state and spending_type=obligation, then sort the returned rows client-side by amount before calling anything a top-state ranking.

suitableQuestions.name: How do recipient-location and place-of-performance geographies differ?
suitableQuestions.description: Compare the same DEFC and spending_type across different scope values to see where money was received versus where work was performed.

suitableQuestions.name: Which geographies have the highest disaster spending per capita?
suitableQuestions.description: Use the returned per_capita metric to compare geography burden or concentration where population is available.

notSuitableFor.name: Award-level or transaction-level detail
notSuitableFor.description: The endpoint returns aggregates by geography and does not include award identifiers, recipient names, or transaction records.

notSuitableFor.name: General federal spending outside disaster-designated funds
notSuitableFor.description: The request is anchored on DEFC filtering, so it is not the right surface for all-spending geographic analysis.

notSuitableFor.name: Trend analysis over time in a single response
notSuitableFor.description: The response grain is geography only with no time bucket dimension, and this repair's sampled time_period passthrough probe did not materially narrow the rollup.

notSuitableFor.name: Recent-only or recipient-bounded geography stories via shared passthrough filters
notSuitableFor.description: A 2026-05-15 live probe accepted filter.time_period, recipient_scope, and recipient_locations but still returned the same nationwide DEFC L state pattern as the unbounded baseline, so those shared filters are not a reliable contract for bounded geography analysis on this endpoint.

notSuitableFor.name: End-to-end semantic DEFC translation entirely inside the promoted MCP surface
notSuitableFor.description: This bundle can safely drive geography totals, but the reviewed promoted semantic surface did not expose a promoted semantic DEFC reference tool. Plain-language DEFC labeling currently requires an explicit external/raw fallback to GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ or the published reference documentation.

joins.to: reference geography tables or external map shapes
joins.description: Map or enrich the returned geography rows by joining shape_code to the appropriate geography reference for the selected layer.

workflows.name: Translate DEFC codes before storytelling
workflows.description: Resolve raw disaster fund codes into authoritative public-law labels before turning geography aggregates into plain-language stories. In the reviewed promoted semantic surface, this translation step is not currently available as a promoted semantic endpoint/tool, so the lookup below is an explicit external/raw fallback rather than an in-surface semantic step.

steps.action: Start with the DEFC codes you plan to send in filter.def_codes. Treat values such as L as opaque identifiers until you translate them through the DEFC reference.

Use GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ as an external/raw fallback to look up each DEFC code and capture its public_law, title, urls, and disaster grouping before writing narrative labels or user-facing legends. Do not assume this lookup is presently available through a promoted semantic MCP tool in the same surface.

Then call this geography endpoint with the same filter.def_codes and carry the externally resolved DEFC labels alongside the returned geography measures so maps and rankings describe the disaster funding in plain language.

workflows.name: Map first, drill down second
workflows.description: Use this endpoint to identify high-spending geographies, then reuse the same DEFC filter with non-null state shape_code values translated into downstream award-search location filters.

steps.action: Call this endpoint with filter.def_codes, geo_layer, scope, and spending_type to identify notable geography rows. Prefer geo_layer=state as the strongest verified path; if you choose county or district, mark the result as documented-but-not-reverified. Use geo_layer_filters when you need to keep a map view bounded; do not rely on shared filter.time_period or recipient-location passthrough keys for recent-only or same-state bounding here.
Sort the returned rows explicitly by amount, per_capita, or award_count before presenting a ranked list because the response order is not a ranking contract.

For state-level follow-up, keep the same filter.def_codes and map each non-null state shape_code into a downstream award-search location object such as {"country":"USA","state":"MD"}. When this endpoint used recipient_location scope or its default, place those objects under recipient_locations with recipient_scope=domestic; when this endpoint used place_of_performance scope, place them under place_of_performance_locations with place_of_performance_scope=domestic.

Insert that filter block into the downstream award-search request template (for example POST /api/v2/search/spending_by_award/) and do not translate the uncoded null shape_code bucket into a state filter because it is not a usable state code.

caveats.statement: The staged markdown internally disagrees about whether the POST body is a string or an object; live probes confirm you must send the object form shown in the example body.
The response can include an uncoded aggregate bucket with null shape_code and display_name when geography assignment is missing and geo_layer_filters are omitted.
DEFC validation is case-sensitive and not uniform across bad inputs: lowercase values returned 400 while an empty array returned 422.

The live templates use raw DEFC codes such as L. Resolve those codes through GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ or the published DEFC reference before turning a query into a plain-language disaster or public-law story, and treat that lookup as an external/raw fallback until a promoted semantic DEFC reference surface exists. In the staged reference, L maps to Emergency P.L. 116-123, Coronavirus Preparedness and Response Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2020, in the covid_19 group.

A 2026-05-15 live probe accepted filter.time_period, recipient_scope, and recipient_locations but still returned the same nationwide DEFC L state ordering and leading amounts as the unbounded baseline, so do not rely on those shared passthrough filters for recent-only or recipient-bounded stories on this endpoint.

The 2026-05-15 live probe returned California ahead of larger Maryland, Virginia, District of Columbia, and Massachusetts rows, so the results array is not a ranking contract and must be sorted client-side before publishing top-geography lists.

County and district layers and face_value_of_loan remain documented but not reverified in this repair, so current live confidence is strongest for state-level obligation and outlay stories and callers should warn before treating county or district as equally validated.

validateRequest should warn for geo_layer county or district and for spending_type face_value_of_loan because those request paths remain documented but not re-probed in this bundle even though they are still transport-valid.
